title: Internal Hom commutes naturally with scheme open restriction
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and U an open of Y. Let F be restriction of module sheaves to the open subscheme U. Internal Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom] admits isomorphisms F(Hom(A,B)) ≅ Hom(FA,FB) for every pair of Y-module sheaves A,B, natural under precomposition A′ → A and postcomposition B → B′. No local freeness or finiteness is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 20.42.3, ordinary internal Hom restriction in its construction

proof.text: Restrict to the over-U site using overHomObjIso. Apply the over-open equivalence and the internal Hom comparison internalHom_overEquiv. Conjugate source and target using overFunctorEquiv U: the inverse comparison is used contravariantly in the first argument, and the forward comparison covariantly in the second argument. The two inverse identities follow from homObjMap composition and the component isomorphism identities.

Compose the naturality square for overHomObjIso_naturality with the naturality of internalHom_overEquiv, then the naturality of overFunctorEquiv. Associativity identifies the composite square with the required equation. This is a sheaf-level statement, with no complex or differential involved, and the same construction works on the empty open and zero sheaves.

proof_origin.description: B3: proved by composing the existing over-site comparisons and the Mathlib natural isomorphism overFunctorEquiv.

lean.statement:
theorem internalHom_restrict_scheme {Y : Scheme.{u}} (U : Y.Opens) :
    let F := Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι
    ∃ s : ∀ A B : Y.Modules,
      F.obj (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf) A B) ≅
        SheafOfModules.homObj (R := U.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf) (F.obj A) (F.obj B),
      ∀ {A A' B B'} (f : A' ⟶ A) (g : B ⟶ B'),
        F.map (SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf) f g) ≫
            (s A' B').hom =
          (s A B).hom ≫ SheafOfModules.homObjMap
            (R := U.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf) (F.map f) (F.map g)
